Read the skill at /home/giak/aidd-device-work/2026-10-24-055310-shadow-areas-design/framework-origin/plugins/aidd-refine/skills/03-shadow-areas/SKILL.md and use it on this repository.
This repository is `cartes-de-visite`, a static business-card project; the artifact to scan is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-01-carte-visite-v2-design.md`.
Run the skill on that artifact, in the order its own actions prescribe, and write the report where its action 02 says; do not modify the source, do not write anywhere else, and do not ask me a question.
I'll start by reading the skill file and the target artifact.

The skill says: before running an action, read its file in `actions/`, not only the table or assets. So I need to read actions/01-detect.md and actions/02-render-report.md, plus references.

Let me list the skill directory.
The skill requires reading each action file before running it. Let me read the actions and references.

Now let me follow action 01: Load, Validate, Handle edges, Scan, Dedupe, Return.

Validate: source is docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-01-carte-visite-v2-design.md inside working directory, not named *-shadow-report.md. Good. It's markdown. No warnings needed.

Check whether a prior report exists (dispatch: with no prior report run detect then render-report; with one, detect then diff). Let me check for an existing shadow report.

Now scan the artifact. Let me read the artifact carefully again and also look at the repo context (maybe useful but the skill says scan the artifact; I shouldn't invent). Let's check for prior reports and repo structure.

commande: cd /home/giak/aidd-device-work/2026-10-24-055310-shadow-areas-design/terrain && ls docs/superpowers/specs/ && git status --short && git log --oneline -3

text:
No prior report. So run detect then render-report.

Now scan the 7 categories in order against the spec. Let me do that carefully, honestly, citing snippets.

Let me re-examine the artifact in detail.

Content:
- 90×55mm card, 2×5 grid, 10 per A4.
- Border 0.5pt around each card as cut mark.
- No rules inside the card.
- Typography: L1-2 EB Garamond small caps; L3 Montserrat light, uppercase with letterspacing; L4 EB Garamond small caps smaller.
- Calibration: ratio 0.88, baseW 210px, baseF 34px, scale 340px = 90mm.
- Algorithm given in pseudo-code.
- Deliverables HTML, PDF, SVG, optional README.
- Constraints: @page A4, margins ~5mm; Google Fonts; PDF must embed glyphs; all #000 on #fff; URL text strictly giak.substack.com with CSS uppercase.
- Success criteria: PDF printed; 10 cards cuttable, legible, no text truncated; pyramid visible; nothing else on card.
- Out of scope: recto-verso, QR, colors, other formats, other publications.
- History.
- References: v1 files, about page, mockups.

Now find genuine gaps.

Category 1: unstated assumption.
Candidates:
a) Assumption that Google Fonts is reachable at generation time / fonts load before PDF print. Actually constraint says fonts loaded via Google Fonts and PDF embeds glyphs (chrome headless does it). The assumption that headless Chrome waits for webfonts before printing is a real unstated assumption — known failure: fonts not ready → fallback font → wrong metrics → pyramid broken. That's a genuine implicit condition. Snippet: "Polices chargées via Google Fonts (EB Garamond + Montserrat) ; le PDF doit embarquer les glyphes (chrome headless le fait)." Severity: major? If assumption wrong, calibration collapses; rework. Not necessarily blocker since work can start. I'd say major.
b) Assumption that the printed output is monochrome-safe: "Laser B&N, 100% noir sur blanc pur" and "aucune grisaille" — assumption that the printer's halftone/antialiasing of thin text stays pure. Hmm, more of an edge/failure. Maybe skip.
c) Assumption that card is single-sided and no bleed — margin 5mm "suffisant" as cut margin. Assumption that cutting by hand along 0.5pt border yields exact 90×55. Hmm, actually the border is at the card edge, and cards are adjacent in a 2×5 grid — so where do cut lines go? With 10 cards in 2 columns × 5 rows touching each other, adjacent borders overlap; cutting through means shared lines. There's an ambiguity: is the 0.5pt border the trim line (cut on it) and do cards share edges? Actually that's a real gap: "bordure fine 0.5pt autour de chaque carte (repère de coupe)" — if cards share edges, a single cut separates two cards, and the border sits on the cut line so it may be cut away or remain on both. Also "marge de coupe suffisante (~5mm autour de la grille)" leaves no gutter between cards. This is an unstated assumption or missing edge case. I'd class as unstated assumption: that adjacent cards share the border line and a single straight cut serves both. Snippet: "bordure fine 0.5pt autour de chaque carte (repère de coupe)" + "marge de coupe suffisante (~5mm autour de la grille)". Hmm, two snippets; choose the border one.

Also assumption: user prints at 100% scale ("100% noir sur blanc pur" is about ink coverage, not scale). Actually "Impression | Laser B&N, 100% noir sur blanc pur" — the "100%" refers to black coverage. But there's a real unstated assumption that the PDF is printed at actual size / no "fit to page" scaling. Since PDF is A4 and page A4, scaling is likely but printers often default to "fit". That's an unstated assumption affecting the 90×55mm dimension. Severity: major (rework at print). Probe: "Does the print workflow require the PDF to be printed at 100% scale with 'fit to page' disabled?" — must start with a locked form. "Should the printing instructions state that the PDF must be printed at 100% scale with fit-to-page disabled?" starts with "should" ✓. Snippet: "Laser B&N, 100% noir sur blanc pur." Hmm the snippet is about black. Maybe snippet: the @page constraint. This is a legit gap since dimension accuracy is the whole point.

Category 2: ambiguous term.
a) "plus « carrée »" in Contexte — vague, but context not critical → minor. Snippet: "La v2 est plus minimale, plus « carrée », limite LaTeX." Ambiguous term: what does "carrée" mean (geometric? typographic? composition?). Both interpretations → same implementation? Not really, but it's in context narrative, minor.
b) "limite LaTeX" — ambiguous: does it mean "bordering on LaTeX-like" or "limite" as in boundary? Minor.
c) "marge de coupe suffisante (~5mm autour de la grille)" — "~5mm" approximate while layout must be exact for 90×55 at 10 per page. A4 = 210×297. Grid 2×5: width 2×90=180mm, height 5×55=275mm. Margins: (210-180)/2 = 15mm horizontal, (297-275)/2 = 11mm vertical if centered. So "~5mm autour de la grille" is factually inconsistent with a centered grid: minimum available margin is 11mm vertically, and you can't have 5mm around a 180×275 grid within A4 (that would need 190×285, fits actually: 180+10=190 ≤210, 275+10=285 ≤297). So 5mm margin is feasible but then the grid isn't centered: leftover 20mm horizontal, 12mm vertical. And the latest commit says "insets verticaux symétriques (11mm)". So the spec's "~5mm" is ambiguous/underspecified: is 5mm a minimum, an exact value, or does the grid get centered? This is genuinely ambiguous and affects implementation (where the grid sits on the page). Severity: major? It affects cutting margin and centering; two reasonable implementations differ (5mm exact vs centered 11/15mm). Severity major per rubric "ambiguous term used in a critical path where two reasonable interpretations lead to different implementations". Hmm, is it critical path? It determines the print sheet layout; both produce valid printable A4. Rework is minor (reposition). I'd call it major because it caused a doc/implementation mismatch (commit shows 11mm). But rubric says don't escalate speculatively. Two interpretations → different output files → likely rework. I'll say major.

d) "letter-spacing (cap 0.42em)" — cap in em relative to what? Actually clear enough (max 0.42em). Minor ambiguity: 0.42em of the line's font-size — inferable.
e) "Taille de base L1 : 34px (~25.5pt)" — px to pt at 96dpi: 34px × 0.75 = 25.5pt ✓ consistent. Fine.
f) "L3 : Montserrat light, majuscules espacées" — "espacées" (spaced) is quantified by algorithm. OK.
g) "small caps" — EB Garamond small caps: does the font provide true small caps (OpenType smcp) or faux small caps synthesized by the browser? That matters hugely for metrics/calibration and for the PDF glyph embedding. Genuine ambiguity: "EB Garamond small caps" — real design decision: use `font-variant: small-caps` (synthetic in Chrome? Chrome supports smcp if font has it; EB Garamond has smcp? EB Garamond does have real small caps in some versions). If synthetic, lowercase→scaled uppercase. This is a real ambiguous term with implementation consequences. Severity: major. Probe: "Should 'small caps' be implemented with the font's OpenType smcp feature or with synthetic scaled capitals?" Starts with "should" ✓.

Category 3: missing edge case.
a) Longest line vs target widths — algorithm handles overflow by shrinking; but what if shrinking to minimum still exceeds target (no floor specified)? Edge case: line cannot fit target even at very small size. Actually algorithm loops reducing size until natural ≤ target; for a single word it will eventually fit. But no minimum legibility floor → risk of unreadable L1. Edge case: what's the minimum acceptable font size? Hmm.
b) Cards at page edges: first/last card borders at 5mm margin — printer non-printable area often ~4-5mm; edge case of cards near the printer's unprintable margin. Could be missing edge case or failure mode. Snippet "marge de cut suffisante (~5mm)". This overlaps with (c) above; pick one.
c) What if the pyramid must hold for a different name/URL length (e.g., name longer than target)? Out of scope says other publications, but the name is fixed. Skip.
d) Missing edge case: URL line is the only lowercase→uppercase transformed line; "GIAK.SUBSTACK.COM" at 163px target with letter-spacing — if the natural width exceeds at the artificial spacing, handled. Skip.
e) Edge case: 10 cards means 2 columns × 5 rows exactly on A4 297mm: 275mm + margins. Fine.
f) Edge case: blank/whitespace line? No.
g) Edge case: text truncation criterion "aucun texte tronqué" — how verified? That's acceptance criterion.
h) Edge case: What if the printer adds a margin so the outermost cards' cut border is clipped (marge ~5mm vs unprintable area)? I'll use as missing edge case: outermost card borders fall within the printer's non-printable margin. Actually "marge de coupe suffisante (~5mm)" directly claims sufficiency; the edge case is a printer with larger unprintable area. This is arguably missing edge case (boundary condition at page edge) → major.

Category 4: missing actor.
Who does what? The doc is a design spec for one user (Christophe) who is also the implementer? Actors: the person printing/cutting (the user), the implementer, the browser (Chrome). Missing actor candidates:
a) No actor is named for the print-and-cut verification: "PDF A4 imprimé en laser B&N : 10 cartes découpables, lisibles" — who prints, cuts, and verifies? The success criteria are only verifiable by a physical print, and no actor/role is assigned to that verification. Is that a genuine missing actor? Rubric: "A required actor is absent and no decision can be made about their role" → blocker. Hmm, this is a solo project; the user is implicitly both. Declaring blocker would be excessive/speculative. In a solo personal project, the actor is obvious — that's precisely the "unstated assumption" case rather than missing actor. Careful: categories counter-example says an actor mentioned but not detailed isn't missing actor. I think a fair missing-actor gap: the PDF/SVG generation depends on a local Chrome binary and Google Fonts access — that's a dependency, not actor.
b) Missing actor: no owner/reviewer for the "décision de finition à l'implémentation" (L33: "la signature peut être légèrement décalée vers le bas pour respirer (décision de finition à l'implémentation...)"). Who decides the finish offset? It's left to "l'implémentation" — an unnamed actor. If implementer ≠ designer, the visual outcome is unowned. Probe: "Who decides the final vertical offset of the signature block if the implementer and the designer differ?" This is a legit missing actor but in solo project it's minor. Hmm. Rubric blocker says actor absent and no decision can be made. Here a decision can be made (implementer decides). So minor/major. I'd say minor.

Maybe better: is there any real "missing actor"? The spec never names who performs the measurement calibration (canvas mockup) vs who hardcodes values. Meh.

I'll include one: the finish decision (signature vertical offset) has no named decision-maker. Severity minor.

Category 5: missing failure mode.
a) Google Fonts unreachable / font fails to load → fallback font → pyramid and metrics wrong, PDF silently wrong. This is a genuine failure mode: "Polices chargées via Google Fonts … le PDF doit embarquer les glyphes". The doc asserts it works but doesn't say what to do if a font 404s or network is offline during generation. Real: headless Chrome offline → fallback. Severity: major. But is it duplicate with the unstated-assumption (a) about fonts loading before print? Different: assumption = Chrome waits for fonts; failure mode = network unavailable / font request fails. I should avoid double-counting same issue. The skill dedupes by category+snippet; same snippet different category would be two gaps, which is allowed but a bit redundant. Better to keep one: the failure mode (font load failure → silent fallback) is more actionable. And keep the unstated assumption about something else. Hmm.

Let me reconsider assumptions list to avoid overlap:
- Assumption 1: that the PDF will be printed at 100% scale (no fit-to-page) → dimension fidelity. Snippet: "@page : A4, marges telles que la grille 2×5 (90×55mm) tienne avec marge de coupe suffisante (~5mm autour de la grille)". Hmm that snippet overlaps with ambiguous "~5mm". Use "Impression | Laser B&N, 100% noir sur blanc pur." for print assumption? The 100% there refers to black. Using it for scale is a stretch but the snippet is the "Impression" row. I could use the criteria line "PDF A4 imprimé en laser B&N : 10 cartes découpables". Eh.

Let me instead use a stronger assumption: the calibration assumes measured widths from a 340px mockup scale to mm linearly, i.e., that Chrome's px→pt→mm mapping and font rendering at print DPI match the canvas measurement at mockup scale. That's a real, consequential unstated assumption: canvas measureText at 34px vs PDF print at 25.5pt — hinting/rounding differences mean the "measured" widths won't reproduce exactly. If wrong, the pyramid widths drift. Severity: major. Snippet: "La pyramide est calibrée par **mesure réelle** (canvas `measureText`, polices chargées)" or "ces valeurs sont converties en pt/mm à l'implémentation avec le même algorithme". Good — that's distinct from font-loading failure.

- Assumption 2: that "bordure 0.5pt" is a cut guide and cards share edges (single cut serves two cards) — actually more of a missing edge case/ambiguity. Let me classify the sharing/no-gutter issue as "missing edge case"? Hmm. Definition: boundary condition not covered. Cards adjacent with zero gutter is a boundary condition of the layout: what happens to the shared border between two adjacent cards? I think "missing edge case" fits better than assumption. But I also want an edge case for printer margin. Two edge cases is fine.

Let me now be concrete and build the gap list with snippets, categories, severities, probes.

Proposed gaps:

unstated assumption
1. [major] Calibration assumes canvas-measured widths at 340px mockup scale reproduce identically in the print PDF (px→pt→mm, hinting). Probe: "Does the calibration assume that widths measured with canvas `measureText` at 34px will reproduce identically in the printed PDF at 25.5pt?" — must be a question starting with a form; "Does …" ✓. Snippet: "La pyramide est calibrée par **mesure réelle** (canvas `measureText`, polices chargées)".
   Hmm probe style: shortest actionable. Maybe: "Are the canvas-measured widths guaranteed to match the printed PDF widths after px→pt→mm conversion?" starts with "are" ✓.
2. [major] Assumes print at 100% scale / no fit-to-page. Probe: "Should the printing instructions require 100% scale with fit-to-page disabled?" Snippet: "Impression | Laser B&N, 100% noir sur blanc pur." Reasonable: the Impression row is where print settings belong but only ink is specified.
3. [minor] Assumes cutter/print path is one person + that the "décision de finition" owner = implementer? That's missing actor. Skip.

Actually, is #2 an assumption or missing acceptance/dependency? "Assumption, if wrong, invalidates a core design decision" — 90×55 dimension is core. Fit-to-page would shrink cards ~4-5%. Rework: major. Fine.

ambiguous term
1. [major] "small caps" — true OpenType vs synthetic. Snippet: "Lignes 1-2 : EB Garamond small caps." Probe: "Which small-caps implementation applies to lines 1-2: the font's OpenType smcp feature or synthetic scaled capitals?"
2. [major] "~5mm autour de la grille" — exact vs minimum vs centered. Snippet: "@page : A4, marges telles que la grille 2×5 (90×55mm) tienne avec marge de coupe suffisante (~5mm autour de la grille)." Probe: "Is the ~5mm cut margin a fixed offset or a minimum that yields a centred 180×275mm grid with 15mm/11mm insets?" Hmm long. "Is the ~5mm cut margin a fixed value or a minimum around a centred grid?"
3. [minor] "plus « carrée »" — context only. Snippet: "La v2 est plus minimale, plus « carrée », limite LaTeX." Probe: "What does « carrée » mean concretely for the v2 composition?" — hmm probe must start with locked form ✓ "what".
4. [minor] "letter-spacing (cap 0.42em)" — em relative to which size? Probably inferable → minor. Maybe skip to avoid noise. I'll include? The skill says emit one gap per distinct issue; minor noise is acceptable but quality matters. I'll include the "cap 0.42em" as minor only if genuinely ambiguous — 0.42em is clearly relative to the element's font-size. Not a real gap. Skip.

missing edge case
1. [major] Adjacent cards share a single border line / zero gutter between cards: the 0.5pt "repère de coupe" sits between two cards, so cutting it leaves no guide margin and the border may be clipped on one side; also 2 columns touching. Snippet: "bordure fine 0.5pt autour de chaque carte (repère de coupe)". Probe: "How are shared borders between adjacent cards cut so that each finished card keeps its 90×55mm edge?" Starts "how" ✓. Severity major (surfaces in physical test).
2. [major] Outer cards fall inside the printer's non-printable margin: no gutter, cut margin ~5mm = typical unprintable ~4-5mm; edge case where the 0.5pt outline is unprintable. Probe: "Will the 0.5pt border on the outermost cards survive the printer's non-printable margin?" starts "will" ✓. Snippet: "marge de coupe suffisante (~5mm autour de la grille)". Hmm overlapping with ambiguous #2 same snippet. Dedupe rule: same category and snippet → one gap. Different categories → allowed. But two gaps on the same snippet is repetitive. Maybe drop the ambiguous ~5mm one and keep the edge-case one? The ambiguity is genuinely about centering. I'll keep the ambiguity (about centering) and reframe edge case 2 to be about the printer's unprintable area with snippet from "Impression" row? Better: snippet "Laser B&N, 100% noir sur blanc pur" doesn't fit. 

Alternative edge case: what if a line's natural width exceeds its target even after shrinking to the floor — no minimum size floor defined. Probe: "What is the minimum legible font size before the shrink loop stops for line 1?" Snippet: "si natural_i > target_i : réduire size_i (pas de 0.5px) jusqu'à natural_i ≤ target_i, ls=0". That's a genuine edge case (no floor) and distinct. Severity major? Would cause rework if illegible. But natural width for "RÉSISTANCE" at 34px: roughly 10 chars × ~0.6em ≈ 204px at 34px... target 210 → letter-spacing needed. So no shrink likely. The floor is unlikely to bind. Severity minor. Hmm, "Do not assign major speculatively". Missing edge case that will surface in testing → major. But if it never binds, minor. I'd say minor.

Better edge case: line 3 URL must remain strictly "giak.substack.com" but displayed uppercase; CSS text-transform uppercase — the glyph widths change with uppercase, so the calibration measured on uppercase? The algorithm measures "ligne_i" — but is the measured string the lowercase source or the uppercase display? That's a genuine edge case/ambiguity in calibration: measureText on the raw text vs the CSS-transformed text. If you measure lowercase and display uppercase, target width breaks. That's a strong, concrete gap — could be "missing edge case" or "ambiguous term". I'd call it missing edge case? It's a boundary of the measurement step (input not covering transform). Definition of missing edge case: "A boundary condition or exceptional input that the described behavior does not cover." Hmm, this is more an unstated assumption that measureText uses transformed text. I'll classify as unstated assumption: "the algorithm's measureText input is the rendered (uppercase, letter-spaced) string". Snippet: "natural_i = measureText(ligne_i, size_i)" plus the URL constraint. Actually choose snippet line 59: "Le texte de l'URL doit rester strictement `giak.substack.com` (affichage en majuscules via CSS `text-transform`, pas de substitution du texte)." Probe: "Does the calibration measure the URL string as rendered in uppercase, or as the lowercase source text?" ✓ starts "Does". Severity: major (breaks L3 width if wrong → rework). Good, and it's a real spec flaw.

So unstated assumption gets 3: canvas/print fidelity, print scale, measurement input string.

missing actor
1. [minor] Who owns the finish decision (vertical offset of signature)? Snippet: "la signature (L3 + L4) peut être légèrement décalée vers le bas pour respirer (décision de finition à l'implémentation, sans bouger l'axe horizontal)". Probe: "Who approves the vertical offset of the signature block at implementation time?"
2. Maybe missing actor: no named verifier of the physical print test. Probe: "Who performs and signs off the physical print-and-cut test?" Severity: major? In a solo project the user is the actor; naming them changes nothing. Per rubric "A required actor is absent and no decision can be made about their role" → but decision can be made. I'll assign minor... Actually is it a genuine gap? The success criteria require physical verification; nobody is designated. For a solo project, that's the user. I think emitting it as minor is defensible and honest. Hmm, but it risks being "vague feedback". I'll include just one actor gap (the finish-decision owner) to stay sharp. Actually the physical verification owner is more consequential for "done". Let me include both? Two actor gaps: (a) verifier of print test [major? no, minor], (b) finish-decision owner [minor]. To reduce noise, include only (a)? 

Honestly the strongest actor gap: no one is named as the person who prints and cuts, and the "10 cartes découpables" criterion only exists physically. In a solo project, minor. I'll include one actor gap combining? No — rule 3: one specific gap per probe. I'll pick the finish-decision owner as it's explicitly deferred ("décision de finition à l'implémentation") — that's an actual unnamed decision-maker. And add the print verifier as minor too? I'll include both but keep them distinct and short. Hmm. Let me decide: include 2 minor actor gaps? That may feel padded. I'll include just the deferred finish decision (explicitly deferred = clearest missing actor) and the print verification actor as major? No.

Decision: one actor gap, minor: finish-decision owner.

missing failure mode
1. [major] Google Fonts unreachable/blocked during PDF generation → silent fallback font → pyramid and metrics wrong, PDF ships anyway. Probe: "What should happen when a Google Fonts request fails during PDF generation?" Snippet: "Polices chargées via Google Fonts (EB Garamond + Montserrat) ; le PDF doit embarquer les glyphes (chrome headless le fait)."
2. [major] Chrome headless not installed / version differs → `--print-to-pdf` fails or prints differently; no fallback path named. Snippet: "HTML/CSS → PDF via `google-chrome --headless --print-to-pdf` (même chaîne que v1)." Probe: "What is the fallback when google-chrome is absent or a different version changes the print output?" Hmm combine two — split: "What is the fallback when google-chrome is not installed on the generation machine?" Severity: major? For a solo local project, minor/major. Failure discovered at generation → rework. I'd say minor if v1 proves the chain works. Actually v1 already used it, so low risk → minor. But missing failure mode → "will be discovered during integration and require a code change" → major. Since v1 exists and works, the chain is proven → minor. I'll say minor.
3. Missing failure mode: Chrome doesn't wait for webfonts → PDF with fallback. This is a variant of #1; keep #1 only, mention fonts not ready? Dedupe: same category+snippet → one gap. Keep #1.
4. Missing failure mode: printer driver applies scaling/greyscale — overlaps assumption #2. Skip.
5. Missing failure mode: text truncation at card edge despite criteria "aucun texte tronqué" — how to detect? That's acceptance criterion.

So failure modes: fonts fail [major], chrome missing [minor].

missing acceptance criterion
1. [blocker]? "Pyramide inversée visible à l'œil nu" — not testable: no measurable definition (e.g., each line ≥ X% narrower, or measured widths within tolerance). This is a described behavior with no pass/fail. Severity: major (not blocker, since design can proceed; but verification impossible → per rubric "An acceptance criterion is missing and there is no other way to confirm done" = blocker). Hmm. Two criteria: "Pyramide inversée visible à l'œil nu sur la carte imprimée." That's subjective. The calibrated widths give objective data (55.6/48.9/43.0/37.9), so you can verify from the file. So there IS another way to confirm → major, not blocker. Good: major.
2. [major] "10 cartes découpables, lisibles, aucun texte tronqué" — "lisibles" undefined (min font size / min x-height), "aucun texte tronqué" has no tolerance/check method. Snippet: "PDF A4 imprimé en laser B&N : 10 cartes découpables, lisibles, aucun texte tronqué." Probe: "What minimum printed font size defines « lisible » for the four lines?" starts "what" ✓. Severity major.
3. [minor] "cohérente avec l'A4" for the SVG deliverable — no criterion of what coherence means (same metrics? same ratios?). Probe: "Which measurements must the standalone SVG match to count as coherent with the A4 sheet?" Severity minor (documentation clarity; implementation produces SVG from same numbers). Maybe major? It could produce a divergent SVG. I'd say minor.
4. Acceptance criterion for the border "0.5pt" — is it exactly 0.5pt in PDF? minor. Skip.
5. Missing acceptance: "Pyramide" criterion duplicates #1.

missing dependency
1. [major] Google Fonts CDN dependency for EB Garamond + Montserrat: version/pinning, offline availability, and whether fonts are vendored locally. Probe: "Which exact font versions or files are required, and are they vendored locally or fetched at build time?" — combines two. Split: "Are the EB Garamond and Montserrat files vendored locally or fetched from Google Fonts at generation time?" Snippet: "Polices chargées via Google Fonts". But that's the same snippet as failure mode #1. Different category, fine. Hmm — instead use failure mode snippet same. It's okay per dedupe rules. But to keep report clean, maybe make dependency gap about the mockup assets: the calibration references `.superpowers/brainstorm/...` mockups and v1 files — the implementation depends on those mockup files existing to re-measure, and they live in a `.superpowers` brainstorming dir that may be transient/untracked. That's a genuine missing dependency: the calibration values can't be reproduced without those mockups. Probe: "Are the brainstorm mockups under `.superpowers/brainstorm/...` retained and tracked, since the calibration cannot be reproduced without them?" Snippet: "Mockups de brainstorming : `.superpowers/brainstorm/1306592-1785595127/content/`". Severity: major? It's a reproducibility dependency; values are documented in the spec so re-measure isn't strictly needed. Then minor. Hmm — but the algorithm says "à répliquer" (must be replicated), which requires the measurement harness. Actually the spec says print sheet doesn't need canvas because values are hardcoded. So mockups are only needed if recalibration is required → minor.
2. [major] dependency: google-chrome headless binary + version — that's failure mode already. Dependency gap: Chrome version/DTP printing behavior not pinned. Could double count. Skip.
3. Dependency: Substack about page as reference for content — is the URL confirmed live? The URL giak.substack.com must match the about page. Not really a build dependency.
4. Dependency: PDF generation requires local Chrome; if the repo is shared/CI, no CI image named. Minor. Overlaps #2 failure mode.
5. [major] dependency: no named tool for SVG generation (deliverable 3: `v2/carte_de_visite.svg`). The technique row only specifies HTML/CSS→PDF; nothing says how the SVG is produced (hand-written? exported from mockup? same measurement pipeline?). That's a genuine missing dependency/missing how. Probe: "How is `v2/carte_de_visite.svg` produced so its metrics match the calibrated A4 sheet?" starts "how" ✓. Severity major (implementer must invent a pipeline → rework risk). Good — that's a real gap: the SVG deliverable's production method is unnamed.
